subject: Warmup lock contention in reserved fleet 1 mitigation & service bridging
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Eleni Markos <eleni@aurorapay.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Aug 2028 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Warmup lock contention in reserved fleet — quick mitigation and short continuity plan

Eleni,

We detected a warmup lock contention event impacting your reserved fleet (apparent in us-west-2 fleet id: rn-usw2-fleet-07) beginning ~07:50 PDT. Symptoms: large spikes in request queuing and elevated 99th latency for churn-heavy chat routes while many clients attempted first warmup concurrently. A subset of requests experienced transient 502/timeout errors.

Immediate actions we've taken:
- Applied temporary service-bridging: affected chat routes were routed to your secondary reserved nodes to maintain throughput while we stabilize allocations.
- Reduced concurrent warmup attempts across the fleet to limit allocator lock contention.
- Marked critical webhook routes as exempt from concurrency limits per your prior configuration.
- Collected detailed traces and allocator logs (attached).

Short asks for AuroraPay:
- Please confirm any additional mission-critical routes that must be exempted from concurrency caps.
- If you can forward a few representative client request IDs where you saw timeouts, that helps correlate traces.

Expected timeline: the bridging and throttles should restore steady-state behavior within 1525 minutes. We will continue to monitor and will follow up with a root-cause and postmortem within 24 hours.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Attachments: fleet-warmup-sample-traces-20280824.txt (text)

From: Eleni Markos <eleni@aurorapay.com>

Date: Fri, 24 Aug 2028 08:12:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Warmup lock contention in reserved fleet — quick mitigation and short continuity plan

Ben 1 thanks for the rapid response.

We observed client errors for our /v1/chat/txn-verify route starting at 07:50. Attached are two request IDs (r-9f2b, r-9f2c) and a short heap of samples sent to infra@. We appreciate the bridging; our traffic is spiky at the hour boundary.

One ask: can you confirm whether bridging will preserve ordered delivery for our webhook acknowledgements? Those must remain at-least-once and in timestamp order where possible.

Eleni
VP Engineering, AuroraPay
eleni@aurorapay.com

(Their reply included the request ID list in a forwarded internal trace email.)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Aug 2028 08:22:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Warmup lock contention in reserved fleet — quick mitigation and short continuity plan

Ben 1 see below for ops notes.

Ops diagnostic summary (in-flight):
- Trigger: a flag rollout last week reduced the warmup-buffer reserve for reserved fleets to improve utilization. Under bursty inbound traffic the allocator scheduled many concurrent warmups and hit a lock path in the placement controller.
- Effect: placement controller latency rose, which blocked worker attachment and led to request queueing.
- Mitigation applied: lower warmup concurrency limit, enable service-bridging for affected tenant routing, and exempted critical webhook routes.

Next steps to resolution:
1) Roll our warmup-buffer flag to previous thresholds (target: within 2 business hours) to stop aggressive concurrent warmups.
2) Harden allocator lock with a fast-path fix (owner: infra team, INF-7301).
3) Add a short-term canary to detect repeat signature on reserved fleets.

For AuroraPay1s ordered delivery question: service-bridging will preserve request order within a routed session; webhooks will be proxied through the standby nodes with at-least-once guarantees. We'll provide a brief technical note for your infra team.

Lauren
Sr. Manager, Platform Reliability
lauren@redwood.com

Attachment: service-bridging-checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Eleni Markos <eleni@aurorapay.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Aug 2028 09:05:33 -0700
Subject: Re: Warmup lock contention in reserved fleet — quick mitigation and short continuity plan

Eleni, Ben 1 quick technical follow-up:
- We validated request IDs r-9f2b and r-9f2c in the allocator trace; both experienced a placement wait of ~6.1s before client retry. Those traces are in the attached sampler.
- Bridging keeps ordering by proxying to standby nodes in the same tenant session shard; it does not change message timestamps. If you need stronger ordering semantics we can present a short change to route affinity.

Operational ETA update:
- Stabilization through bridging: immediate (completed).
- Rollback of warmup-buffer flag: planned and scheduled; expect completion by 10:45 PDT.
- Postmortem and long-term fix ETA: 24 hours, with an engineering patch on the allocator scheduler targeted in next sprint.

Aditya Rao
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

Attachment: fleet-warmup-sample-traces-20280824.txt (text)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Aug 2028 10:53:00 -0700
Subject: Update: stabilization complete and next steps

Eleni,

Quick update1 stabilization is complete. The rollback of the warmup-buffer flag completed at 10:42 PDT and allocator placement latencies returned to baseline within ~8 minutes. We've left the service-bridging in place for an additional hour as a safety buffer, then will remove it if metrics remain stable.

Action items for next 24 hours:
- We'll publish a short technical note for your infra team describing the bridging proxy behavior and ordering guarantees.
- Postmortem will be shared in 24 hours and include crediting guidance if SLAs were breached.

Thanks for the fast collaboration. Please ping me directly if you notice any regressions.

Ben

Attachment: None

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Eleni Markos <eleni@aurorapay.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Aug 2028 14:17:00 -0700
Subject: Postmortem: warmup lock contention event (rn-usw2-fleet-07)

Eleni,

Attached is the postmortem PDF with timeline, root cause, and our remediation commitments. High-level summary:
- Root cause: a performance-optimized warmup-buffer rollout reduced reserved-fleet warmup reserves; concurrent warmup scheduling under a burst triggered lock contention in the allocator placement controller.
- Impact: transient queuing and elevated tail latency for a subset of chat routes; small number of client retries and timeouts.
- Remediation: rollback of the flag (complete), allocator fast-path fix (in progress, INF-7301), new canary metric and alert for warmup contention (deployed), and minor compensatory credits scoped in the postmortem.

We regret the disruption. We'll follow up with a short technical Q&A session if you'd like to review the allocator traces with our SREs.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Attachments: postmortem-warmup-locks-20280825.pdf (pdf)
